newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA-HERMIS PLANS CORPORATE FINANCE MOVE.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA-HERMIS PLANS CORPORATE FINANCE MOVE.

text.p: Lithuania's Hermis Bank said on Friday that it planned to expand agressively into corporate finance and make the country's infant stock market accessible to individual investors by launching investment funds.
"We'll take the problem of financing the investment needs of Lithuanian companies to a new level," Ivo Gueorguiev, deputy chairman of Hermis Bank, told a news conference.
"Until now we have mainly been providing loans. From now on, we will work together with them (companies) to raise equity and provide other forms of debt financing," Gueorguiev said.
He said Hermis would work with firms in the privatisation process, mergers and acquisitions and leveraged buy-outs.
"Investment banking is about the flow of capital and Hermis' goal would be to become one of the major intermediaries in the flow of capital in Lithuania," Gueorguiev said.
Hermis also wanted to help develop the capital market and make it easier for individual investors to participate in the stock market and would try to introduce investment funds.
Brokers often complain that Lithuania's stock market lacks liquidity because of the lack of institutional investors. Lithuania has no investment or pension funds.
Gueorguiev said Hermis would like to launch a fund "as soon as possible," but he did not specify when.
"I think that the market is already ready for such a vehicle," Gueorguiev said.
